title: Microsoft Entra ID Application client secret: one-property twin (boundary)
summary: 3 inputs are identical to a positive input except for one change: the value is cut, extended or delimited so that it no longer ends where the format ends. Legacy mutation notes: marker: 8R~ vs the Q~ marker the provider's Add-MgApplicationPassword examples show at offset 4. Twin of "Microsoft Entra ID Application client secret: must be flagged (provider-documented) [legacy tier T1]".
rationale: A twin changes exactly one property, so the expected outcome differs from the positive for that one reason. Reporting the twin is a false alarm, and it shows that the changed property is part of what identifies the credential.

expectation.rationale: Negative twin of microsoft-entra-client-secret-digit-q-tilde-bare: marker: 8R~ vs the Q~ marker the provider's Add-MgApplicationPassword examples show at offset 4. Exactly one structural property differs from the positive; silence follows from construction.
